Business</font></b></h1> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Recent Developments</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" color=black lang=EN-US>We operate through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Unilens Corp. USA, located in Largo, Florida. We changed our domicile from British Columbia, Canada, where we were incorporated in 1989, to the State of Delaware on April 1, 2010. In June 2010, as a final step in our corporate reorganization, we organized Unilens Vision Sciences Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Unilens Corp. USA, and transferred our principal intellectual property assets and licensing arrangements to that company. Our shares trade on the OTCQX tier of the OTC Markets Group, using the symbol &#147;UVIC&#148;. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We license, manufacture, distribute and market specialty optical contact lens products using proprietary design and manufacturing technology.</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> Our products are sold solely to eye care professionals, primarily in the United States, through in house sales representatives and a network of distributors. Our lens products are marketed as a family of specialty vision correction products that can serve the majority of the population&#146;s vision correction needs. Our specialty optical lens business is divided into four categories: (i) disposable lenses; (ii) custom soft lenses; (iii) gas permeable lenses; and (iv) replacement and other lenses. During the twelve months ended June 30, 2014 our C-Vue disposable products accounted for approximately 53% of our sales.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>&nbsp;On May 23, 2012, we obtained a $3,500,000 5-year term loan facility and a $1,500,000 line of credit with Hancock Bank, which replaced a $6.9 million term loan facility and $1.5 million line of credit with Regions Bank originally obtained in January 2010 to finance the repurchase of approximately 48% of our outstanding shares from our then largest stockholder. The Hancock Bank term loan and line of credit both had a floating interest rate of 30-day LIBOR plus 3.00%. As part of this refinancing, a related interest rate swap with Regions Bank was terminated.&nbsp; Previously, in December 2011, we repaid in full a $279,998 advance under a capital equipment credit facility we had obtained from Regions Bank in April 2011 to finance the purchase of manufacturing equipment for additional production capacity and efficiencies, and terminated that credit facility at that time.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>On October 4, 2013, we repurchased 618,522 shares of our common stock, representing approximately 26% of our total shares outstanding, from our then largest stockholder, Baker Street Capital L.P. The aggregate purchase price was approximately $3.1 million, or $4.97 per share.&nbsp; We funded this stock repurchase through a $3.3 million expansion and modification of our term loan and line of credit facility with Hancock Bank. The amortization of the term loan facility was increased from five to seven years and the line of credit was reduced to a maximum of $750,000.&nbsp; The interest rate on both the term loan and line of credit was increased to a floating rate of 30-day LIBOR plus 3.5%. (See Note 6, Term Loan, Line of Credit and Interest Rate Swap, to our Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report).</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Products and Services</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Our disposable lenses line consists of the C-Vue Multifocal lens, our silicone hydrogel C-Vue&#174; HydraVUE&#153; Multifocal, launched in March 2013, and our new silicone hydrogel C-Vue&#174; ADDvantage&#153; Multifocal for Presbyopia for monthly replacement, launched in June 2014.&nbsp; Our newest product incorporates Unilens&#146; highly advanced, next-generation multifocal contact lens design technology, which allows for ease of fit by providing a consistent near ADD power across all power profiles, ultimately resulting in clear vision for presbyopes at all distances. The lens is also thinner and more rounded at the edges for added comfort. All C-Vue disposable multifocal lenses are cast molded and come in blister-packed boxes of six lenses sold for frequent replacement. Our disposable lenses line also includes the C-Vue Aspheric single vision lens, a single vision disposable soft contact lens sold for frequent replacement and the C-Vue 1 Day Aspheric single vision daily disposable soft contact lens sold for one day wear then just simply thrown</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:12pt face=arial,sans-serif lang=EN-CA> </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>away. C-Vue multifocal lenses are manufactured for us by a third party, utilizing one of our patented soft lens designs, and, is marketed exclusively in the United States to eye care professionals. The cast molded C-Vue Aspheric single vision lens and the C-Vue 1 Day Aspheric single vision lens are each ,manufactured for us by a third party utilizing Wavefront inspired technology. We market the C-Vue Aspheric single vision lens in a blister-packed box of six lenses and the C-Vue 1 Day Aspheric single vision lens in blister-packs of 30 and 90 lenses.&nbsp; </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:center; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font size=2>2</font></p></div> <hr width=100% size=2 noshade align=center> <div style=PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always>&nbsp;</div><a name=page_6><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <div style="PADDING-LEFT:0%; PADDING-RIGHT:0%"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><a href=#TC>Table of Contents&nbsp;</a></font> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Our custom soft lenses line of soft lathe-cut products includes the C-Vue Toric Multifocal, designed for patients with an astigmatism that requires bifocal correction, the C-Vue Custom Toric and the C-Vue 55 multifocal, a high-add multifocal </font></font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>lens manufactured in a comfortable high-water content material, all available in our Advanced line of biocompatible materials. In September 2009, we launched the C-Vue Advanced Toric Multifocal lens in blister-packs for monthly replacement, featuring free trial lenses for practitioners. In January 2011, we launched our C-VUE Advanced&#174; HydraVUE&#153; line of silicone hydrogel custom contact lenses for monthly replacement. This family of silicone hydrogel products incorporates our most highly-developed lens design technology into our Toric Multifocal and Multifocal designs and in our made-to-order Custom Toric and Single Vision options. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Our gas permeable lens line of products consists of the Unilens GP&#153;, a multifocal contact lens intended for patients with astigmatism who need low to moderate presbyopic correction; the Unilens GP Plus&#153;, designed to accommodate wearers requiring higher presbyopic correction; the C-Vue GP, a front aspheric design incorporating the C-Vue design technology and the C-Ray GP utilizing our recently patented design technology, featuring an on eye ray traced power profile over an elliptical base. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Our replacement and other lenses line of products primarily consists of the Unilens&#153;, an aspheric multifocal contact lens; the SoftSite&#153;, a high-add multifocal contact lens; the SimulVue&#153;, a simultaneous vision bifocal contact lens with the capabilities for correcting advanced presbyopia; the Unilens EMA, a visibility tinted multifocal contact lens available in planned replacement modality; the LifeStyle brand of toric multifocal, toric and spherical daily, and extended wear lenses and the Sof-Form single vision lenses marketed under the Lombart brand; the UniVision, an aspheric low vision lens; and the, Aquaflex and SoftCon spherical daily and extended wear brand of lenses acquired from CIBA Vision. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Customers, Sales &amp; Suppliers</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We currently market and distribute our products exclusively to qualified practitioners through a combination of authorized independent distributors, authorized manufactures&#146; representatives, and in house sales representatives.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>In October 2001, we licensed the exclusive worldwide rights to </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>our multifocal soft contact lens design</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> to Bausch + Lomb Incorporated (&#147;Bausch + Lomb&#148;). In April 2013 we extended this licensing agreement and granted Bausch + Lomb an exclusive worldwide license to use our new multifocal technology. Under the agreement, Bausch + Lomb </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>manufactures and markets cast-molded multifocal soft contact lenses using our technologies.&nbsp; We receive a royalty ranging from two to five percent of Bausch + Lomb&#146;s worldwide net sales of these products for as long as it manufactures and sells them. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>During the fiscal years ended June 30, 2014, 2013, and 2012 we recorded $</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:9pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>2,242,925</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>, $</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:9pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>2,089,013</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>, and $</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:9pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>2,539,696</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>, respectively, in royalty income. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>There can be no assurance, however, that Bausch + Lomb will continue to sell products utilizing our technologies in the future.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; TEXT-DECORATION:none; LETTER-SPACING:0pt" face="Times New Roman" color=windowtext lang=EN-US>Our sales are not substantially subject to seasonality, except that sales during</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" color=black lang=EN-US> </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>the quarter ending December 31 are normally lower than other quarters due to a decrease in patient visits to eye care professionals during the Christmas holiday season.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We rely on several suppliers for most of the raw materials used in the production of our soft contact lenses. During fiscal 2011, we began purchasing silicone hydrogel raw material, to which</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> we did not previously have access, </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>from&nbsp;</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> Contamac US, and, in January 2011, </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>we launched the C-Vue Advanced HydraVue family of </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>silicone hydrogel custom contact lenses.&nbsp; </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Except for silicone hydrogel, our raw materials are readily available in our industry and alternate vendors have been identified as potential suppliers with competitive pricing and quality.&nbsp; Over the past three fiscal years, we have not experienced any volatility in the price of raw materials.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>We have a supply agreement with one supplier for the manufacture of our molded C-Vue multifocal lenses. This agreement was amended in February 2013 to include silicone hydrogel multifocal lenses, such as our C-Vue HydraVue silicone hydrogel multifocal lens and our new silicone hydrogel C-Vue ADDvantage multifocal lens.&nbsp; Currently, sales of these multifocal lenses account for approximately 45% of our annual sales.&nbsp; The agreement is renewable from year to year and is terminable pursuant to customary termination clauses. Although to date the supplier has met our requirements, there can be no assurances that it will continue to do so. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Backlog is not a material factor in our business.</font></p><a name=_aciFooter6> <div> <div> <div align=left>&nbsp;</div> <div align=center> <table bordercolor=transparent style=WIDTH:0px cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0> <tr> <td style="PADDING-BOTTOM:0in; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><a href=#TC>Table of Contents&nbsp;</a></font> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Competition</font></b>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" /></div> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We operate within the highly competitive contact lens market.&nbsp; We compete with industry leaders, such as Vistakon, Inc. a unit of Johnson and Johnson Vision Care, Inc., Bausch + Lomb, </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>a unit of</font><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face=arial,sans-serif color=#333333 lang=EN-CA> </font></b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" color=#333333 lang=EN-CA>Valeant Pharmaceuticals International Inc.</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>, </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Alcon Laboratories, Inc., a division of Novartis AG, and Cooper Vision, Inc. a unit of Cooper Companies, Inc. Our ability to compete successfully is dependent in part on eye care professionals&#146; perceptions of product quality, product development, technical innovation, and price. We market our products worldwide.&nbsp; For the fiscal years ending June 30, 2014, 2013, and 2012, approximately 1% of our revenue in each year was derived from sales outside the United States, primarily from sales in Canada, Brazil and England.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The conventional soft multifocal contact lens business has been affected by the introduction of molding manufacturing technology, allowing for the mass production of most lens types at a fraction of the cost to lathe lenses. The entry of these molded lenses into the marketplace has created significant price competition. The reduced cost of the molded lens allows for liberal amounts of trial lenses to be provided to eye care professionals for a more productive fitting session and immediate dispensing of lenses.&nbsp; Furthermore, lower manufacturing costs led to the introduction of frequent replacement and disposable lenses, a modality preferred by many consumers.&nbsp; Recognizing this trend, we signed an agreement with a third party in 2002 for the supply of disposable multifocal molded soft contact lenses (C-Vue) utilizing our patented design. T</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>he C-Vue brand was launched to eye care professionals in the United States during September 2002. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>In&nbsp;</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>February 2013, we amended this agreement to include silicone hydrogel lenses and announced the launch of our then new silicone hydrogel disposable </font><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>C-Vue<sup>&#174;</sup></font></i><b><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> </font></i></b><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>HydraVUE</font></i><b><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>&#153; </font></i></b><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Multifocal </font></i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>contact lens for monthly replacement.&nbsp; In June 2014, we launched our new silicone hydrogel C-Vue&#174; ADDvantage&#153; Multifocal for Presbyopia contact lens for monthly replacement. In February 2006, we announced the launch of the first aspheric, single vision daily wear, frequent replacement disposable soft contact lens available under the C-Vue brand. The C-Vue Aspheric single vision lens is manufactured by a third party utilizing, Wavefront inspired technology. In May 2008, we launched the all-new C-Vue 1 Day ASV, which is the first aspheric daily disposable contact lens sold under the C-Vue brand. The cast molded C-Vue 1 Day ASV lens is manufactured for us by a third party utilizing Wavefront inspired technology, and is marketed to eye care professionals in blister-packs of 30 and 90 lenses</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face=arial,sans-serif lang=EN-US>. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>During fiscal 2014, our C-Vue disposable products accounted for approximately 53% of our sales. We</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB> expect that sales of our disposable category which includes the C-Vue brand </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>multifocal, silicone hydrogel multifocal and ADDvantage multifocal,</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>the C-Vue Aspheric single vision and the C-Vue 1 Day ASV lenses in total </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>will start to make up a greater percentage of our future sales as sales of our C-Vue ADDvantage Multifocal for Presbyopia grow and anticipated new products are launched. We also expect sales of our custom soft lenses will continue to grow and make up a greater percentage of our future sales.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>The aging of the U.S. population indicates that speciality contact lenses will continue to be the fastest growing segment of the contact lens market. Specialty contact lenses include toric, toric multifocal, and cosmetic lenses. We believe that our custom soft specialty lenses, including our C-Vue multifocal lenses for presbyopia, our C-Vue custom toric lens for correcting astigmatism and the C-Vue Advanced toric multifocal lens, will grow over time due to such market demographics favoring specialty lenses, and our patented multifocal technology. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>Our C-Vue Advanced HydraVue family of </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>silicone hydrogel custom contact lenses are part of our increased emphasis on silicone hydrogel products in our soft custom lens business</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>. The contact lens market has experienced a shift in recent years towards molded and lathe cut lenses manufactured with </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>silicone hydrogel materials. In addition to</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB> our new silicone hydrogel C-Vue ADDvantage multifocal lens</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>, we anticipate the launch of new silicone hydrogel disposable lenses within the next twelve months. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We regularly compete with a number of other companies in the contact lens industry that have substantially greater financial resources than we do.&nbsp; Our ability to compete is based upon marketing quality products to eye care professionals utilizing our patented technology.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Government Regulation</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Contact lenses are regulated as medical devices in the U.S., the EU and other countries.&nbsp; In the U.S., all non-exempt devices must receive pre-market approval by the FDA.&nbsp; There are two review procedures to gain this pre-market approval depending on the amount of risk posed by the device: a Premarket Approval Application (&#147;PMA&#148;) procedure and a Section&nbsp;510(k) submission.&nbsp; Under a PMA, the manufacturer must submit to the FDA supporting evidence sufficient to prove the safety and effectiveness of the device.&nbsp; The FDA has 180 days to review a PMA.&nbsp; Certain products, however, may qualify for a submission authorized by Section 510(k).&nbsp; Under this procedure, the manufacturer gives the FDA a pre-market notification that it intends to commence marketing the product, and that it has established that the product is substantially equivalent to another product already on the market.&nbsp; The FDA has 90 days to review a Section&nbsp;510(k) submission.&nbsp; In the EU, the "CE" </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>mark is required for all medical devices sold.&nbsp; We hold a CE mark for the classes of contact lenses that we sell.&nbsp; The CE mark allows us to market products upon signing a declaration of conformity with the EU's Medical Device Directive requirements, which we do for each product sold.&nbsp; In addition, medical device sales in the EU require auditing by a Notified Body to ensure that the manufacturer's quality systems are in compliance with the requirements of the ISO 9000 standards.&nbsp; We have a Notified Body, which routinely audits our quality systems.&nbsp; </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; FONT-WEIGHT:normal" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>See "Item 1A --"Risk Factors" &#150; Our manufacturing facility located in the U.S. and our products sold in the U.S. are subject to stringent regulation by the Food and Drug Administration. See "Item 1A --"Risk Factors". </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Our products are subject to stringent regulation by various foreign jurisdictions in which our products are sold. </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; FONT-WEIGHT:normal" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>The cost of compliance with U.S. and foreign regulatory requirements is significant and, particularly when we introduce new products, may from time to time be material to our business.&nbsp;</font></p><a name=_aciFooter7> <div> <div> <div align=left>&nbsp;</div> <div align=center> <table bordercolor=transparent style=WIDTH:0px cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0> <tr> <td style="PADDING-BOTTOM:0in; PADDING-RIGHT:0%"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><a href=#TC>Table of Contents&nbsp;</a></font> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Research and Development</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We have ongoing research and development activities relating to different contact lens products, other applications of our technology and component materials.&nbsp; Research and development expenditures for fiscal years ending June 30, 2014 and 2013 were $</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>86,286 and</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> $</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; While less expensive, and less time-consuming than obtaining PMA clearance, securing Section 510(k) clearance may involve the submission of a substantive review of six months or more.&nbsp; Any products manufactured or distributed pursuant to Section 510(k) clearance are subject to pervasive and continuing regulation by the FDA, including record keeping requirements and reporting of adverse experience with the use of the device. </font></p><a name=_aciFooter11> <div> <div> <div align=center> <table bordercolor=transparent style=WIDTH:0px cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0> <tr> <td style="PADDING-BOTTOM:0in; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in 1in; TEXT-INDENT:-1in"><b><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM:uppercase" face="Times New Roman Bold"><a name=9>ITEM 7. Management&#146;s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations </font></b></h1> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>The following management discussion and analysis (&#147;MDA&#148;) is based on and should be read in conjunction with &#147;Selected Financial Data&#148; above and our consolidated Financial Statements and Supplementary Data</font></i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> </font><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>(the &#147;Financial Statements&#148;), which begins on page 22.&nbsp; The Financial Statements have been prepared in United States dollars and in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles (&#147;US GAAP&#148;). Unless otherwise indicated, all dollar amounts disclosed in this MDA are expressed in United States Dollars.&nbsp; </font></i></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><i><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Operating results are not necessarily indicative of results that may occur in future periods. The MDA contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. The actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of many factors including, but not limited to, those set forth under &#147;Cautionary Statement About Forward-Looking Statements&#148; and &#147;Risk Factors&#148; in Item 1A., included above in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. All forward-looking statements included in this document are based on the information available to us on the date of this document and we assume no obligation to update any forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</font></i></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:center; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left><font style=FONT-SIZE:8pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>14</font></p></div> <hr width=100% size=2 noshade align=center> <div style=PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always>&nbsp;</div><a name=page_18><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><br><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><a href=#TC>Table of Contents&nbsp;</a></font>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font> <div style="PADDING-LEFT:0%; PADDING-RIGHT:0%"> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Overview</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>We license, manufacture, distribute and market specialty optical lens products using our proprietary design and manufacturing technology.&nbsp; Our products are sold solely to eye care professionals, primarily in the United States, through in </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>house sales representatives and a network of distributors. Our lens products are marketed as a family of specialty vision correction products that can serve the majority of the population&#146;s vision correction needs. Our specialty optical lens business is divided into four categories: (i) disposable lenses; (ii) custom soft lenses; (iii) gas permeable lenses; and (iv) replacement and other lenses. During the 2014 fiscal year,</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB> our C-Vue disposable products </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>accounted for approximately 53% of our sales.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Sales of</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> our specialty optical lens products </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>accounted&nbsp;</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>for the largest percentage of our total revenues, constituting approximately 73%, while royalty income </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>derived from our exclusive license of our patented multifocal designs to Bausch + Lomb</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> was approximately 27% of revenues during the 2014 fiscal year.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Economic conditions in the United States, while improving, have constrained our growth. We are however optimistic about the long-term outlook for the contact lens market and the specialty contact lens market, in particular. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>The aging of the U.S. population indicates that speciality contact lenses will continue to be the fastest growing segment of the contact lens market. Specialty contact lenses include multifocal, toric, toric multifocal, and cosmetic lenses. We believe that our speciality disposable and custom soft lenses will grow over time due to such market demographics </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>favoring</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB> specialty lenses and our patented multifocal technology.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We believe such market demographics will continue to drive our revenue and earnings. In February 2013, we announced the launch of our than new silicone hydrogel disposable C-Vue&#174; HydraVUE&#153; Multifocal contact lens for monthly replacement. The new product continues to incorporate our highly developed, world-class, patented multifocal design technology in a silicone hydrogel material, which offers the benefit of higher oxygen transmissibility for better eye health. In June 2014, we announced our latest silicone hydrogel C-Vue&#174; ADDvantage&#153; Multifocal for Presbyopia for monthly replacement. This new product incorporates our highly advanced, next-generation multifocal contact lens design technology, which allows for ease of fit by providing a consistent near ADD power across all power profiles, ultimately resulting in clear vision for presbyopes at all distances. The lens is also thinner and more rounded at the edges for added comfort.&nbsp; We expect sales from the C-Vue ADDvantage multifocal will steadily increase during the 2015 fiscal year and beyond. In January 2011, we launched our C-VUE Advanced<sup>&#174;</sup> HydraVUE&#153; line of silicone hydrogel custom contact lenses for monthly replacement. These lenses are completely customizable and feature a risk-free trial program.&nbsp; Sales of this lens have grown steadily during the 2012, 2013 and 2014 fiscal years.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>A significant portion of our net income is derived from our exclusive license with Bausch + Lomb and such </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>royalty income is a major component of our profitability. In April 2013, we announced that we had extended our license agreement with Bausch + Lomb. The amended agreement continues to cover the exclusive worldwide license for our multifocal technology and in addition grants Bausch + Lomb an exclusive worldwide license for our new multifocal technology.&nbsp; Under the terms of the arrangement, existing royalty rates will remain in effect and will apply for both technologies. Bausch + Lomb recently introduced the PureVision&#174; 2 for Presbyopia in the U.S., after its earlier introduction in certain European markets.&nbsp; The new addition to the PureVision portfolio incorporates Bausch + Lomb&#146;s own innovative lens technology, using certain licensed elements of our next generation technology. We expect that this new contact lens offering by Bausch + Lomb will help grow our future royalty income.&nbsp;Bausch + Lomb currently sells the Soflens Multi-Focal, the PureVision Multi-Focal, the PureVision 2 Multi-Focal and the Biotrue<sup>&#174;&nbsp;</sup>ONEday for Presbyopia under our license agreement.&nbsp;However, there can be no assurance, that such royalty income from Bausch + Lomb will grow or that Bausch + Lomb will continue to sell products in the future utilizing our technology.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>The contact lens market is highly competitive.&nbsp; We compete with industry leaders, such as Vistakon, Inc. a unit of Johnson and Johnson Vision Care, Inc., Bausch + Lomb, a unit of Valeant Pharmaceuticals International Inc., Alcon Laboratories, Inc., a division of Novartis AG, and Cooper Vision, Inc. a unit of Cooper Vision Companies, Inc.&nbsp; Our ability to compete successfully is dependent in part on eye care professionals&#146; perceptions of product quality, product development, technical innovation, and price. </font><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>We have a supply agreement with one supplier for the manufacture of our molded C-Vue multifocal lens. This agreement was amended in February 2013 to include silicone hydrogel multifocal lenses. Together these lenses account for a significant portion of our sales (approximately 45% during the 2014 fiscal year). The agreement is renewable from year to year and is terminable pursuant to customary termination clauses. Although to date the supplier has met our requirements, there can be no assurance that it will continue to meet its obligations under our agreement or as to any renewal of our supply agreement. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; Net cash used in the 2013 Year was for the purchase of capital additions, primarily manufacturing and inspection process improvements and equipment. </font></p> <h2 style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</h2> <h2 style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman">Financing Activities</font></b></h2> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>On October 4, 2013, the Company funded a 618,522 common stock share repurchase (See Note 8</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US> to our Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>) through a $3,300,000 expansion and modification of our term loan and line of credit facility with Hancock Bank.&nbsp; </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The amortization of the term loan facility was increased from five to seven years and the line of credit was reduced to a maximum of $750,000. &nbsp;The interest rate on both the term loan and line of credit was increased to a floating rate of 30-day LIBOR plus 3.5%, from 30-day LIBOR plus 3.0%. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>&nbsp;The minimum existing monthly principal payments under the Hancock Bank term loan facility are $68,075, plus accrued interest. In addition to monthly principal payments, there is an Excess Earnings Recapture Covenant which could require principal term loan principal prepayments by an amount equal to fifty percent of excess cash flow after taxes and dividends based on a Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 1.50 to 1.00.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Monthly interest only payments are due under the Hancock Bank line of credit, with the maximum borrowings at any time not to exceed the lesser of (i) $750,000 or (ii) a sum equal to 85% of eligible royalty receivables, plus 75% of eligible accounts receivables plus 50% of eligible raw material and finished goods inventory. The maximum borrowing amount under this line of credit facility at June 30, 2014 was $750,000. The line of credit is renewable annually and matures on February 1, 2015.The term loan and the line of credit are secured by a security interest in favor of Hancock Bank in our inventory, accounts receivable, general intangibles, cash and principal United States patent. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>In the Current Year, net cash used in financing activities increased $49,471 to $1,157,397 compared to $1,107,926 in the 2013Year. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>Financing activities during the Current Year consisted primarily of new borrowings from Hancock Bank under the revised</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> term loan and line of credit facilities</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB> and the 618,522 share repurchase at $4.97 per share. Total borrowings were $3,218,791 and the total repurchase price was $3,213,604. In addition, there were repayments under the term loan and line of credit facilities of $719,600 and $100,000, respectively, a net debt addition of $2,399,191 compared to a debt reduction of $681,441 in the 2013 Year. Financing activities for the Current Year also included dividend payments to our stockholders of $342,984 compared to $426,485 in the 2013 Year. The reduction in dividends paid in the Current Year from the 2013 Year was caused by the reduction in the number of our shares outstanding as a result of the share repurchase.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>In the 2013 Year, net cash used in financing activities decreased $570,427 to $1,107,926 compared to $1,678,353 in the 2012 Year.</font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN> Financing activities during the 2013 Year consisted primarily of repayments of $700,000 under our Hancock Bank term loan facility, net new borrowings of $18,559 from our Hancock Bank line of credit and payments of $426,485 for dividends to our stockholders.&nbsp; Estimates</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 5.75pt 0pt 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We prepare our consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, which require management to make certain estimates and apply judgment. We base our estimates and judgments on historical experience, current trends and other factors that management believes to be important at the time the consolidated financial statements are prepared. On a regular basis, we review our accounting policies and how they are applied and disclosed in our consolidated financial statements. While we believe the historical experience, current trends and other factors considered, support the preparation of our consolidated financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles, actual results could differ from our estimates, and such differences could be material. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 5.75pt 0pt 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Our significant accounting policies are discussed in Note 2 to our consolidated financial statements. We believe the following accounting policies include a higher degree of judgment and/or complexity and, thus, are considered to be critical accounting policies. </font></p> <p style="MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Inventory </font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:4.5pt 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Our inventories are carried at the lower of cost or market.&nbsp; Cost is determined on a first-in, first-out basis. Inventory is stated at average cost, which is determined by applying the current average cost to the ending inventory.&nbsp; In addition, we reduce the value of our ending inventory for estimated inventory obsolescence. A continuous cycle count process is the primary procedure used to validate the inventory balances on hand to ensure that the amounts reflected in the accompanying consolidated financial statements are properly stated. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:4.5pt 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p><a name=_aciFooter23> <div> <div> <div align=center> <table bordercolor=transparent style=WIDTH:0px cellpadding=0 cellspacing=0> <tr> <td style="PADDING-BOTTOM:0in; PADDING-TOP:0in; PADDING-LEFT:0in; PADDING-RIGHT:0in" align=left valign=top> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:8pt face="Times New Roman">20</font></p></td></tr></table></div></div> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:right; MARGIN:0in 0.25in 0pt 0in" align=right>&nbsp;</p></div></div> <hr width=100% size=2 noshade align=center> <div style=PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE:always>&nbsp;</div>&nbsp;<a name=page_24> <div style="PADDING-LEFT:0%; PADDING-RIGHT:0%"><a name=_aciHeader24> <div> <div align=left><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>&nbsp;<font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA> <a href=#TC>Table of Contents&nbsp;</a></font>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></div></div> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The accounting for inventory contains uncertainty since we must use judgment to estimate inventory obsolescence. When estimating these losses, we consider a number of factors, which include, but are not limited to, historical usage, shelf life remaining and manufactured date of current physical inventory. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Our total reserve for estimated inventory obsolescence covered by this critical accounting policy was $15,868 as of June 30, 2014. Although we believe we have sufficient current and historical information available to us to record reasonable estimates for estimated inventory obsolescence, it is possible that actual results could differ. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We have not made any material changes in the accounting methodology used to establish our inventory obsolescence and loss reserves during the past three years. Although we believe that the estimates discussed above are reasonable and the related calculations conform to generally accepted accounting principles, actual results could differ from our estimates, and such differences could be material. </font></p> <h2 style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman">Allowance for Doubtful Accounts and Returns</font></b></h2> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt"><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>We record an allowance for doubtful accounts to allow for any amounts that may not be recoverable. This is based on an analysis of our prior collection experience, customer credit worthiness, and current economic trends.&nbsp; Also included with this allowance is an amount for product returns. This is based on an analysis of our history of credit memos issued. Quantitative Information About Market Risk</font></b></h2> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Our operations generally do not employ financial instruments or derivatives, which are market sensitive, and accordingly, we are not exposed to the financial market risks related to such instruments.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; NATURE OF BUSINESS</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The business of Unilens Vision Inc. and subsidiaries (the &#147;Company&#148;) is to develop, license and sell optical products using proprietary design and manufacturing technology.&nbsp; The Company&#146;s products are being sold primarily in the United States through a network of national distributors and in house sales personnel.&nbsp; The Company also licenses through one of its subsidiaries, one of its patented multifocal designs on an exclusive basis to Bausch and Lomb Inc. (&#147;Bausch + Lomb&#148;) (Note 5).</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; TEXT-INDENT:-0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; TEXT-INDENT:-0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>These consolidated financial statements are prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#147;US GAAP&#148;) and in United States dollars.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The significant accounting policies adopted by the Company are as follows:</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="times new roman bold" lang=EN-GB>Consolidation</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>These consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Unilens Vision Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Unilens Corp. USA and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Unilens Vision Sciences Inc.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>All significant inter-company accounts and transactions have been eliminated.</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="times new roman bold" lang=EN-CA><strong>Use of estimates</strong></font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The preparation of financial statements in conformity with US GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amount of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amount of revenues and expenses during the period.&nbsp; Actual results could differ from these estimates.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-INDENT:0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Currency</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>These financial statements are expressed in the Company&#146;s functional currency which is United States dollars, as the Company and all its operations are based in the United States. On and effective April 1, 2010 the Company announced the change in domicile and the continuance of its corporate existence from British Columbia, Canada to the State of Delaware.</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="times new roman bold" lang=EN-CA><strong>Fair value of financial instruments</strong></font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The Company&#146;s financial instruments consist of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, royalties and other receivables, accounts payable, notes payable, line of credit borrowings and accrued liabilities.&nbsp; Unless otherwise noted, it is management&#146;s opinion that the Company is not exposed except for variable rates on notes payable and line of credit borrowings to significant interest, currency or credit risks arising from these financial instruments. On August 6, 2010, the Company entered into an interest rate swap agreement to fix the rates on its then term note. On May 23, 2012, the Company unraveled the interest rate swap and terminated the interest rate swap agreement as part of the Hancock Bank refinancing. Under the terminated interest rate swap agreement for the term note, we received or made payments on a monthly basis, based on the differential between 5.66% and LIBOR plus 4.25% (Note 6). </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Due to their short maturities, the fair value of these financial instruments approximates their carrying values, unless otherwise noted. The carrying amount and estimated fair value of long-term notes payable was $4,423,958 and $4,423,958, respectively as of June 30, 2014. The fair value of long-term notes payable was estimated based on rates currently offered to the Company for debt with similar terms and maturities. There were no outstanding investments in derivative financial instruments as of June 30, 2014 and 2013.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Cash and cash equivalents</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; Receivables are determined to be past due, based on payment terms of original invoices. Cost is determined on a first-in, first-out basis.&nbsp; Inventory is stated at average cost, which is determined by applying the current average cost to the ending inventory. The Company provides reserves for inventory that management believes to be obsolete or slow moving.</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt 0.5in; TEXT-INDENT:0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="times new roman bold" lang=EN-GB>Property, plant and equipment </font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Property, plant and equipment are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation.&nbsp; Plant and equipment and office equipment are depreciated on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful life of the asset, typically five years. Leasehold improvements are depreciated over the shorter of the term of the lease or the estimated useful life of the asset.&nbsp; </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Expenditures for certain maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred, and renewals and betterments are capitalized.&nbsp; Gains and losses on disposals are credited or charged to operations. For US income tax purposes, the Company uses accelerated methods of depreciation for all assets</font><font style="FONT-SIZE:12pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Long-lived assets that are subject to depreciation and amortization are reviewed for potential impairment whenever events or circumstances indicate that carrying amounts may not be recoverable.&nbsp; During the years ended </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>June 30, 2014 </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>and 2013, the Company determined that its property, plant and equipment were not impaired.</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA><br>Other Assets</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The Company provides optometric practitioners with in-office trial lenses to use in marketing programs to facilitate efficient and convenient fitting of contact lenses on their patients. These lenses are provided in fitting sets with our C-Vue trial lenses stored in a sturdy cabinet with the Unilens logo on it. We record the costs associated with the original fitting sets and cabinets to other long-term assets on our Consolidated Balance Sheet. We amortize such costs over their estimated useful lives, estimated to be three years, to selling, general and administrative expense on our Consolidated Statements of Income. At June 30, 2014 and 2013 costs associated with the original fitting sets and cabinets included in other long-term assets, was $401,806 and $349,842, respectively.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; TEXT-INDENT:0in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="times new roman bold" lang=EN-GB>Revenue recognition and discounts</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The Company recognizes revenue on sales of optical products upon shipment, when title passes, and ultimate collection is reasonably assured.&nbsp; At the same time, the Company charges operations for the estimated cost of future returns based on historical experience for the respective product types.&nbsp; The Company offers discounts on its products.&nbsp; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.15pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The amounts charged to operations during the years ended June 30, 2014, 2013 and 2012 were $86,286, $85,332 and $85,404, respectively.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Income per common share</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Basic income per common share is calculated by dividing the income for the year by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the year.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:12pt 0in 12pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Diluted income per common share is calculated using the treasury stock method.&nbsp; Under the treasury stock method, the weighted average number of common shares outstanding used for the calculation of diluted income per share assumes that the proceeds to be received on the exercise of dilutive stock options and warrants are used to repurchase common shares at the average market price during the year. As of June 30, 2014 the Company has 140,000 options outstanding. The effect of the dilutive options adds 12,447 shares to the 1,913,512 basic weighted average shares outstanding resulting in diluted weighted average shares outstanding of 1,925,959.</font></p> <p style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER:avoid; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Stock-based compensation and stock options</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Stock-based payments are recorded using </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" color=black lang=EN-US>the fair value method of accounting for stock options.&nbsp; Under this method, in addition to reflecting compensation expense for new share-based awards, expense is also recognized to reflect the remaining vesting period of awards that had been included in pro-forma disclosures in prior periods. There was no stock compensation expense attributable to stock options charged against income during the years ended June 30, 2014, 2013 and 2012, since no options were granted during those years, and all options outstanding at the beginning of the years were fully vested.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Income taxes</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="BACKGROUND:white; TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Taxes on income are provided in accordance with US GAAP. Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been reflected in the consolidated financial statements. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the differences between the book values and the tax basis of particular assets and liabilities, in addition to the tax effects of net operating loss and capital loss carry forwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in the tax rate is recognized as income or expense in the period that included the enactment date. A valuation </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>allowance is provided to offset the net deferred tax assets if, based upon the available evidence, it is more likely than not that some or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.<br></font></p> <p style="BACKGROUND:white; The core principal of the standard is that revenue should be recognized when the transfer of promised goods or services is made in an amount that the entity expects to be entitled to in exchange for the transfer of goods and services. ASU 2014-09 also requires disclosures enabling users of financial statements to understand the nature, amount, timing and uncertainty of revenue and cash flows arising from contracts with customers. This standard will be effective for financial statements issued by public companies for annual reporting periods beginning after 15 December 2016. Early adoption is not permitted. The adoption is not expected to have a material impact on the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt; TEXT-INDENT:0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; ROYALTY AGREEMENT</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>On October 26, 2001, we licensed the exclusive worldwide rights to our multi-focal soft contact lens design to Bausch + Lomb.&nbsp; As part of the Hancock Bank refinancing, the Company expensed $51,638 of loan costs associated with the previous Regions Bank term loan facility and line of credit which is included in other expense in the June 30, 2013 year.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>Also as part of the Hancock Bank refinancing the previous interest rate swap with Regions Bank was unraveled and the interest rate swap agreement was terminated. In addition, the Company reclassified into earnings in the June 30, 2013 year, all of the unrealized losses on the cash flow hedge included in accumulated other comprehensive loss.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>On October 4, 2013, the Company funded a 618,522 common stock share repurchase (See Note 8) through a $3,300,000 expansion and modification of the existing term loan and line of credit provided by Hancock Bank. The aggregate purchase price was approximately $3,074,054, or $4.97 per share.&nbsp; The repurchased shares were returned to the Company&#146;s treasury and subsequently cancelled, leaving 1,750,832 shares outstanding.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>The Company funded the common stock share repurchase through a $3.3 million expansion and modification of the existing term loan and line of credit provided by Hancock Bank (See Note 6).&nbsp; Costs related to the stock repurchase were $84,015, and were charged to stockholders&#146; equity while costs related to the expansion and modification of the existing term loan and line of credit, were $55,535, and were charged to deferred loan costs which are amortized over the life of the amended 7-year term loan facility.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 6pt; TEXT-INDENT:0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>Preferred stock</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 6pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>The Company has no preferred stock issued. In the event the Company issues one or more series of preferred stock, the relative designations, powers, preferences, rights, qualifications, limitations and restrictions of the shares will be determined and set forth in an amendment to the Company&#146;s Certificate of Incorporation.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 6pt; TEXT-INDENT:0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>Common stock</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:12pt 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>On and effective April 1, 2010 the Company completed the change in domicile and the continuance of its Corporate existence from British Columbia Canada to the State of Delaware, which resulted in authorized capital of 30,000,000 common shares with a par value of $.001 per share and 3,000,000 preferred shares with a par value of $.001 per share. The term of any option granted under the Stock Option Plan may not exceed 10 years.&nbsp; </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>The exercise price of each option must equal or exceed the market price of the Company&#146;s stock as calculated on the date of grant. </font><font style="FONT-SIZE:10pt; LETTER-SPACING:-0.1pt" face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>&nbsp;Options, in general, vest immediately except for options granted to consultants performing investor relations activities, vest at a minimum over a period of 12 months, 25% at the end of each three-month period.&nbsp; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The Company uses the Black-Scholes pricing model to estimate the fair value of stock-based awards. The expected volatilities are based on the historical volatility of the Company&#146;s stock price. Historical data is used to estimate option exercises and employee terminations within the valuation model. The expected term of options granted is based on historical exercise patterns of employees and represents the period of time that options granted are expected to be outstanding. The risk-free interest rate for periods within the contractual life of the option is based on the U S Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant. Forfeitures are estimated at the time of grant and revised, if necessary, in subsequent periods if actual forfeitures differ from those estimates. </font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; CONCENTRATIONS</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Credit risk</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in">&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Financial instruments, which potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash investments and trade receivables.&nbsp; The Company places its temporary cash investments with a high credit quality financial institution.&nbsp; Concentrations of credit risk with respect to uncollateralized trade receivables are limited due to the Company&#146;s large number of customers and their geographic dispersion.&nbsp; The Company uses an allowance for doubtful accounts on an item-by-item basis to cover any collectability issues.&nbsp; As a consequence, concentrations of credit risk, which could subject the Company to a loss are limited and are consistent with management&#146;s expectations as reflected in the consolidated financial statements.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:6pt 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-GB>A significant portion of the Company&#146;s net income is derived from the Company&#146;s exclusive license of one of its patented multifocal designs to Bausch + Lomb.&nbsp; The Company collects royalties based on Bausch + Lomb&#146;s worldwide net sales of products utilizing the Company&#146;s technologies.&nbsp; There can be no assurances that Bausch + Lomb will continue to sell products in the future utilizing the Company&#146;s technologies.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in" align=left><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>Volume of business risk</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>The Company has a supply agreement with one supplier for the manufacture of its molded C-Vue multifocal, C-Vue Hydravue and the new C-Vue ADDvantage multifocal lenses, which accounts for approximately 45%, 46% and 49% of the Company&#146;s annual sales during years the years ended June 30, 2014, 2013 and 2012, respectively.&nbsp; The agreement is renewable from year to year and is terminable pursuant to customary termination clauses. </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>The Company has concentrations in the volume of purchases it conducts with this supplier. For the year ended June 30, 2014, purchases from this supplier accounted for approximately 16% of the total cost of goods sold by the Company (2013-17%, 2012-10%).&nbsp; At June 30, 2014, the Company owed this supplier approximately $201,000 (2013- $133,000). </font><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-CA>There is no assurance that an alternate supplier can successfully manufacture these lenses to the Company&#146;s specifications, on acceptable terms, or within the constraints of the exclusive license agreement with Bausch + Lomb.</font></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt"><b><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>11.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; REVENUE INFORMATION</font></b></p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:left; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt" align=left>&nbsp;</p> <p style="TEXT-ALIGN:justify; PADDING-LEFT:0px; MARGIN:0in 0in 0pt 0.5in"><font style=FONT-SIZE:10pt face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US>All of our assets and operations are located in the United States in one business segment. Our revenues are derived from royalty income received from our exclusive agreement with Bausch + Lomb for the use of our patented multifocal designs and technology, and from sales from our specialty optical lens business, which manufactures and distributes optical products that use our proprietary design and manufacturing technology.
